name: Customer finder prompt guide
description: The customer finder prompt from the reel: Claude searches job ads for small businesses that are advertising for what you sell, scores each one, and drafts a first message from their own ad.

page.title: Find businesses that already want to pay for what you sell
page.sub: One free prompt from the reel. A business that is advertising a job for what you do already wants to pay for it. Claude finds those ads, scores each business out of ten, skips the recruiters, and writes a short first message using a real detail from the ad.
page.prompt_how: Paste this into a Claude chat with web search switched on (the free plan has it). Change the part in square brackets first.
page.prompt_note: Open every ad before you write to anyone: job boards show cached pages, so an ad can be old or already filled.
page.tested_title: We ran it ourselves, for a bookkeeper

results.name: It found 6 real small businesses advertising for a bookkeeper
It skipped 5 staffing agencies and said so
One ad named its own budget: $600 a month
A first message for each, from a detail in the ad
Whether each ad is still open (it could not confirm the dates)

page.tested_text: We ran it in a normal Claude chat for a sample online bookkeeping service (from $300 a month). It came back with **6 small businesses** that were advertising for a part-time or contract bookkeeper, including a tree service paying **$30 an hour** and one that had named a budget of **$600 a month**. It skipped **5 staffing agencies** and told us it could not confirm how old each ad was. It wrote a first message for each one from a real detail in the ad. **Not checked:** whether the ads were still open, and nothing was sent to anyone. **One thing that did NOT work:** we first asked it to find people asking for a bookkeeper on Reddit. Claude can't read Reddit at all, so this guide doesn't promise that.
page.tip: **The tip:** say your price in the brackets. When an ad names a budget, Claude compares the two and tells you who to contact first.

prompt:
You are my customer finder. I sell: [what you sell, who it is for, your price, your country or city]. A business that is advertising a job for the thing I sell is a business that already wants to pay for it. Search the web right now for small businesses that are advertising for a part-time, freelance or contract [job title that matches what you sell] in the last 30 days. Use real job listings only (company career pages, Indeed, LinkedIn Jobs, Craigslist, local job boards, anything you can actually open).

For each one give me: the business name, what it does and where, the job title, the pay or hours if the ad says, the date posted if shown, the link, a fit score from 1 to 10 with a one-line reason (small company and part-time hours score highest, big companies and full-time roles score lowest), and a short friendly opening message I could send the owner that offers my service as a cheaper, faster alternative to hiring, using one real detail from their ad.

Rules: only listings you actually found, each with its link. Never invent a business, a number or a date. If a detail is not in the ad, write 'not stated'. Skip recruiters, staffing agencies and big companies. Give me the 10 best in a table ranked by score, then tell me which three to contact first and why. If you find fewer than 10 real ones, give me fewer.

followups.label: Find the owner
followups.prompt: For the top three, find the owner's or manager's name and a public contact route from the business's own website. Give me the link for each. If you can't find one, say so.
followups.note: Only from their own site. Never guess an email address.

followups.label: A second message
followups.prompt: Write a short, polite follow-up for each of the three, to send a week later if I hear nothing. Under 60 words, no pressure.

followups.label: Run it every week
followups.prompt: Run the same search again and show me only ads you did not list last time: [paste last week's table]

checklist.title: Fill in the brackets
checklist.detail: What you sell, who it is for, your price and where you work. Then the job title a business would hire for instead of buying from you.

checklist.title: Paste it into Claude
checklist.detail: A normal Claude chat with web search on. It takes about a minute.

checklist.title: Open every ad
checklist.detail: Check that it is real, recent and still open before you do anything else.

checklist.title: Send it yourself
checklist.detail: Use the message as a start and rewrite it in your own voice. Claude sends nothing.

checklist.title: Keep the table
checklist.detail: Save it, so next week you can ask for new ads only.

safety: **Check every ad yourself.** Claude told us it could not confirm posting dates. An ad can be months old.
**One message, then stop.** Write to a business once, perhaps follow up once, and take no for an answer. Follow the rules of the site you contact them through.
**It can get details wrong.** Compare the message with the ad before you send it.
